resources.string:
This measures the shape of each stick's gate and works out limits that reach full scale in every direction, including the diagonals. 

The gate is not round — about 84% on this hardware — so the sticks will reach full output at roughly 85% of their physical travel. That is the price of the diagonals working, and it is unavoidable on a gate this shape. 

Takes about a minute. Nothing is written until you have seen the result.
Let go of both sticks and leave them alone. Measuring where they rest, and how much they move on their own.
Roll the stick slowly all the way round, pressed hard against the outside of its travel. Two or three laps. The marked sectors are the ones still short.
Let go again. A stick does not return to quite where it started, and the difference is what sets the deadzone.
The orange contour is where output reaches full scale. Inside the measured shape everywhere means every direction saturates.
Roll both sticks round again. These readings come from the framework, the same numbers a game sees — a stored calibration that is not in effect fails here.
Root required. Add this app in Magisk → Superuser → + (Magisk 31 never prompts), then reopen.
The joystick node is missing — this is not an AYN Thor running a kernel that exposes it.
